The main organizational structure of the Eticas AI Risk Taxonomy is a three-level hierarchy consisting of 10 top-level categories, 21 sub-groups, and 70 active subcategories. This structure is designed to provide navigable and bounded scopes for audit teams, allowing for coherent assessment areas with distinct methodologies. Each subcategory is defined where a single test protocol applies, ensuring operational test scope is clear and manageable.

In contrast, the IBM AI Risk Atlas organizes risks by lifecycle stage (input, inference, output, non-technical, and agentic) and integrates with a tooling suite for compliance workflows. This lifecycle organization aligns with development workflows but complicates compliance crosswalks, as it does not focus on risk-domain organization like the Eticas taxonomy. The Eticas taxonomy emphasizes audit-oriented granularity and operationalization, while the IBM Atlas is more focused on lifecycle stages and automated detection, which may underweight governance and process controls.
